subject: TracerBridge SDK coalition kickoff — integration sprint plan
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@tracerbridge.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Cc: partner@tracerbridge.io
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TracerBridge x Redwood — SDK + tracing shim proposal

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick intro call today. As promised, attaching our SDK spec and a lightweight proposal for a joint integration sprint. High-level ask: we’d like to build an official TracerBridge adapter that plugs into Redwood’s serving runtime to surface fine-grained LLM trace events (token-level latencies, kernel choices, quantization fallbacks) and optionally emit spans to customers’ tracing backends.

Key outcomes we’d propose for a 3-week sprint:
- Deliver a LangChain + LlamaIndex friendly adapter and an opt-in runtime shim for Redwood Dedicated and Hosted runtimes.
- Verify trace fidelity across short/long context workloads and generate sample dashboards.
- Draft a small joint marketing announcement + integration docs.

I attached tracerbridge-sdk-spec.pdf and a draft SOW (draft-sow-tracerbridge-redwood.docx).

Would you and your engineering partner(s) be available for a 60-minute kickoff next week to align on acceptance criteria, security checklist, and which customer use-cases we prioritize?

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Developer Partnerships
TracerBridge

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@tracerbridge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TracerBridge x Redwood — SDK + tracing shim proposal

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the materials, they’re clear and actionable. Quick answers and next steps from our side:

1) Kickoff: We can do Tue 11/02 10:30 PT (we have a 60-min slot). Please confirm and we’ll send a calendar invite.
2) Team: I’ll own the project on the product side. Marissa will lead SDK compatibility (LangChain/LlamaIndex) and Evelyn will run security/compliance gating for Dedicated customers.
3) Security: before any code runs in a Dedicated environment we’ll need your dependencies list, SCA report (or SBOM), and a brief design doc on what data is emitted to tracing backends. Can you include those in the Drive doc?

Marissa / Evelyn — FYI, Sanjay’s attachment includes the initial spec and SOW. Marissa, can you look at where this would live in our SDK surface (LangChain connector vs separate npm/pypi package)? Evelyn, please flag any immediate compliance blockers.

Sanjay — please confirm the kickoff time and share a Google Drive link to the spec if easier.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Integrations & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@tracerbridge.io>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TracerBridge x Redwood — SDK + tracing shim proposal

Adding a few engineering notes after skimming the SDK spec:

- LangChain & LlamaIndex compatibility: we should aim for an adapter pattern where TracerBridge supplies a middleware that can be inserted into the Redwood SDK runtime pipeline. That gives us compatibility with both LangChain chains and LlamaIndex query flows without forcing customers to change their code.
- Runtime footprint: ask for a sample binary size and a memory usage profile for token-streamed workloads. If the shim impacts our per-GPU memory after KV cache, we’ll need quantization-aware options.
- Trace schema: Sanjay, can you confirm if you can map your span schema to OpenTelemetry semantic conventions? We prefer OTEL-compatible events (resource + span attributes) to minimize downstream integration work for customers.

I’ll scope the engineering story for the kickoff and list initial acceptance tests (adapter importability, no-op mode, OTEL export, 95th-pctl overhead <= 8ms per-token on sample benchmark).

-Marissa
Senior SDK Product Manager
Redwood Inference

---

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@tracerbridge.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>, partner@tracerbridge.io
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TracerBridge x Redwood — SDK + tracing shim proposal

Thanks — Tue 11/02 10:30 PT works for our engineering and product leads. Invite accepted.

Quick answers to Marissa’s bullets:
- Adapter pattern & LangChain/LlamaIndex: yes, we can deliver a thin middleware that registers token callbacks and exposes a simple Python/TS API. We’ll provide examples for LangChain Agents and the LlamaIndex Retriever flow.
- Runtime footprint: we’ll attach a 2-page memory/CPU profile to the Drive doc; the default instrumentation adds ~3–5% CPU and ~60MB RAM for long-context 8k tests. There’s an \"opt-out\" build that strips runtime metrics for more constrained hosts.
- OTEL: TracerBridge already supports OpenTelemetry; we’ll map spans to OTEL attributes and provide a compatibility shim.

I’ve uploaded the spec and a draft SOW to the Drive: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-tracerbridge-kickoff

Attachments included in the thread: tracerbridge-sdk-spec.pdf, draft-sow-tracerbridge-redwood.docx

We’ll bring an initial acceptance-test checklist to the kickoff and a minimal test harness that runs on Redwood Dedicated dev instances. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Sanjay
Head of Developer Partnerships
TracerBridge
